passage:
Seema: You used to say you just go on stage and it works. What changed?

Charu: A dead laptop, honestly. Two years ago mine died five minutes before a client talk and I stood there sweating. Now when I rehearse, I picture the good version, sure, but I also run two bad ones. One: the laptop dies. Two: someone asks, "Why is your number so different from last year?" For the first, I keep the slides on paper in my bag. For the second, I wrote a short answer on a card: what the number includes, and what I will check and send by evening. Last month the cable failed, I handed round the printouts, and nobody blinked.

Seema: And the tough question?

Charu: It came. The card was enough.

qa.q: What does Charu carry in case the laptop dies?
qa.a: Charu keeps the slides on paper in the bag.

qa.q: How did Charu feel when the laptop died two years ago?
qa.a: Charu felt panicked and anxious, standing there sweating five minutes before the client talk.

qa.q: What else could Charu prepare for?
qa.a: Charu could prepare for losing the slides file by keeping a copy on a memory stick or emailed to the host.

qa.q: How might the audience have seen the printouts when the cable failed?
qa.a: The audience might have seen Charu as calm and well prepared, since nobody blinked and the talk carried on.

grounding: Shows a presenter adding rehearsals of a dead laptop and a hard question, then carrying printouts and a prepared answer.

passage:
I'm Sachin, and I've sat in on a lot of Himani's client presentations at the agency. Last month she did something new, and I noticed.
The day before the pitch, she didn't just run through her slides. She ran through them twice. The first time, everything went smoothly. The second time, she said, "Now the laptop dies at slide three," and carried on talking from memory, using only a paper printout of her slides on the table.
Then she asked me to throw the hardest question I could think of. I asked, "Why should we trust a new agency with our launch?" She fumbled a bit, then wrote a three-line answer and practised it twice.
On pitch day, the laptop worked fine. But the client's director asked almost exactly my question. Himani answered calmly, in three lines. I don't know if she was nervous. She looked steady.

qa.q: What question did Sachin ask Himani?
qa.a: "Why should we trust a new agency with our launch?"

qa.q: What does Himani looking steady during the client's question suggest?
qa.a: It suggests she felt prepared and confident, having practised that answer, though Sachin can't be sure how nervous she was.

qa.q: What else could Himani rehearse before her next pitch?
qa.a: She could practise what to do if the client cuts the time in half, so she knows which slides to skip.

qa.q: How might the client's director see Himani's answer?
qa.a: The director may be impressed by the calm, clear reply and see the agency as prepared and trustworthy.

grounding: It shows a presenter rehearsing both success and a dead laptop and a tough question, carrying printed slides and a short prepared answer.

passage:
Monday. Chaitanya's big pitch to the hospital board was on Friday. Last year, in his first pitch, the projector cable had failed and he had frozen. His teammate Joseph still joked about it.
Tuesday. Chaitanya did his normal run-through, slides and all. Then he did something new. He closed the laptop halfway through and said out loud, "Laptop's dead. Now what?" He stumbled. So he printed the slides, six to a page, and tried again with only the paper. Better.
Wednesday. He asked Joseph to play the grumpiest board member. Joseph asked, "Why should we pay for this when the old system works?" Chaitanya had no good answer. He wrote one, three sentences, and rehearsed it until it sounded natural.
Friday. Halfway through, the screen flickered and went black. Chaitanya picked up his printout and kept going without a pause.

qa.a: He printed the slides, six to a page.

qa.q: How might Chaitanya have felt when the screen went black on Friday?
qa.a: He may have felt a brief jolt of fear, but also calm and ready, since he had practised with only the printout.

qa.q: What else could Chaitanya prepare for next time?
qa.a: He could rehearse what to do if the meeting is cut short, choosing the three slides that matter most.

qa.q: How might Joseph see Chaitanya's pitch this time?
qa.a: Joseph may be impressed and proud of his teammate, seeing him keep going without a pause after last year's freeze.

grounding: It shows a presenter rehearsing a dead laptop and a tough question, carrying printed slides and a short prepared answer.
